title: United States Semiquincentennial Commission Amendments Act of 2020
official_summary:
United States Semiquincentennial Commission Amendments Act of 2020

This bill modifies certain requirements of the U.S. Semiquincentennial Commission, which was established to provide for the commemoration of the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States and related events.

Among other things, the bill

  • modifies the membership requirements of the commission;
  • changes the date by which the commission shall report to the President with its specific recommendations for the commemoration of the 250th anniversary and related events to March 31, 2020; and
  • grants the commission the exclusive right to use, and to allow others to use, the official marks, imprimaturs, and logos of the commission.

summary.headline: A 2020 law changes how the U.S. Semiquincentennial Commission is set up, when it reports, and who may use its official logos.
summary.what_it_does: The law updates rules for the commission that plans commemorations of the nation's 250th anniversary. It changes the commission's membership requirements. It moves the date for the commission's recommendations to the President to March 31, 2020. It also gives the commission the exclusive right to use its official marks, imprimaturs, and logos, and to permit others to use them.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the U.S. Semiquincentennial Commission
who_it_affects.how: Their membership requirements are changed by the law.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses and organizations that want to use the commission's official logos or marks
who_it_affects.how: They need the commission's permission to use its official marks, imprimaturs, and logos.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 31, 2020. The summary does not list a separate effective date.
